speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Fatima, thank you for joining us. Is it a good moment?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, the little ones are napping and the big ones are at school, so I have maybe forty minutes.

speaker: interviewer
text: Perfect, we'll be done well before that. There are no wrong answers.

speaker: interviewee
text: Okay, inshallah.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: We are six. Me, my husband Youssef, and four children, from three to twelve. I do the shopping and the cooking, he does the car and the bins. I go to the wholesale place once a month for the big things, and the supermarket every week for fresh.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: A neighbour. She said the prices are the same as in the store, so I wanted to check if that's true, because with six people, every bit matters.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Walk me through your last Shmuber Eats order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: I made the list on paper first, like always, then I typed it in. Rice, a lot of rice, chicken, lentils, vegetables, milk, eggs, bread, butter. I compared the prices with my paper from the store. Mostly the same, some higher.

speaker: interviewer
text: And putting things away, anything notable?

speaker: interviewee
text: It was a lot of bags. The driver was nice, he helped me carry them to the door.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe once a month now. For the heavy things. Rice, oil, water.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: I plan by recipe, for the week. I write the dish and what it needs. Last time it was my daughter's birthday cake, and I'd written unsalted butter for the buttercream, and the picker sent a tub of margarine instead, the soft one for toast, and the icing just slid off the cake.

speaker: interviewer
text: Oh no, margarine for buttercream? What did you do?

speaker: interviewee
text: I sent Youssef to the corner shop at eight in the evening for real butter. He was not happy. The cake was okay in the end.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did you get a choice about that swap, or did it just arrive?

speaker: interviewee
text: It just arrived. On the screen it said spread, so maybe for them butter and spread are the same thing. For baking, no.

speaker: interviewer
text: That's really helpful, thank you. Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: Apart from the butter? The chicken was a bigger pack, so it cost more. I would prefer they ask first, because of the budget.

speaker: interviewer
text: Would you have answered if they'd asked?

speaker: interviewee
text: At home, yes. If I'm doing the school run, no, I'm driving.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I chose ten to twelve, when the small ones nap. If it comes at the wrong time, they wake up with the doorbell and then my whole day is finished.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: If I ordered every week, yes. But once a month, no, it's not worth it. Maybe three, four.

speaker: interviewer
text: What about 9.99 with free delivery?

speaker: interviewee
text: 9.99 for one delivery a month? No. That is more than the delivery fee.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: For the heavy things, yes. For fresh, I still like to choose myself.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What did you like most?

speaker: interviewee
text: Not carrying the rice. Twenty kilos, with four children, that is a job.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: That the prices are not always the same as the store, like the neighbour said. Some things are a bit more.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how was it overall?

speaker: interviewee
text: Seven.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe one thing. Twice the driver came at the very end of the two hours, and the baby was awake by then. If I could pick a smaller time, even a cost, that would help me.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it, noted. Thank you so much, Fatima, this was very helpful.

speaker: interviewee
text: You're welcome. Bye bye.
